blocks.0x70000000:
Trap table (TBR = 0 at reset, 0x70000000 during POST). Slot 0 is the reset
vector; every other slot is  sethi/or %l4 ; jmp %l4 ; rd %psr,%l0  to a POST
handler (%l1/%l2 = PC/nPC of the trapped instruction, %l0 = PSR).
blocks.0x70001000:
post_entry: first POST instruction (reached by jmp 0x70001000 from
reset_power_on). Disables SBus arbitration (MID register = 0), sets
PSR = 0x10e0 (EF, S, PS, ET), TBR = 0, initialises ttya, reports a pending
watchdog reset (system control bit 4), flushes the TLB, clears the cache
tags, context = 0, context table pointer = 0, then post_main.
blocks.0x7000109c:
Default POST trap handler. If the trap type (TBR.tt) equals %g5 (the trap the
running test expects) clear %g5 and return past the trapping instruction
(jmp %l2 ; rett %l2+4); otherwise report_sync_trap.
blocks.0x70001104:
Window overflow (tt 5): WIM = ror(WIM,1), save into the window to spill, store
its 16 registers with stda [%sp+n] 0x20 (MMU bypass: the POST stack is
physical), restore, retry the save (jmp %l1 ; rett %l2).
blocks.0x70001178:
Window underflow (tt 6): WIM = rol(WIM,1), restore twice, reload 16 registers
with ldda [%sp+n] 0x20, save twice, retry the restore.
blocks.0x700012ac:
trap_irq01 .. trap_irq15 (tt 0x11-0x1f): accept the interrupt if tt equals %g5
(expected trap) or %g6 (expected interrupt), otherwise report_async_trap. Then
clear this level's soft interrupt (bit 16+level in the processor 0
Clear-Pending register 0x71e00004), read the pending register back, and do the
per-sub-test work selected by %g7.
blocks.0x70001e3c:
Software trap 0x80: if expected, executes ta 0x80 again with traps disabled,
which puts the IU in error mode (watchdog reset). No POST code issues it.
blocks.0x70001e64: Software trap 0x81: if expected, return past the ta. Unused.
blocks.0x70001eb0:
fp_exception (tt 8): must be expected (%g5 = 8). Drain the FP queue: st %fsr to
the absolute address 0x2100, and while FSR.qne (bit 13) std %fq to 0x2108.
Clear %g5 and return past the FP instruction on which the deferred trap was
taken (so that FP store never executes).
blocks.0x70001f1c:
Unexpected interrupt / asynchronous trap: read AFAR (0x10001004) and AFSR
(0x10001000), clear AFSR, print "Async Trap, PSR, PC, TBR", AFSR and AFAR, and
end the POST with "Replace CPU Board" (post_exit_soft_reset(2, ...)).
blocks.0x70001f80:
Unexpected synchronous trap: read SFAR/SFSR (ASI 4 0x400/0x300), print
"Sync Trap, PSR= PC= TBR=", SFSR and SFAR, end the POST with "Replace CPU
Board".
blocks.0x70002140:
post_main: PSR = 0x10e0, TBR = 0x70000000, WIM = 2, globals cleared. Sizes
memory (mem_size_banks -> %g2), puts %sp at first-bank-base + 0xc00,
re-initialises ttya and the keyboard channel, scans the keyboard for Stop (0x01)
and d (0x4f), detects the keyboard type, and chooses diagnostic mode
(%g4 bit 1), silent mode, or skipping the POST.

blocks.0x70002b44:
FPU CEXC tests (this one and the following eleven): FSR = 0x0f800000 (all IEEE

must not reach memory, and the FSR cexc bit must be set.

blocks.0x700075e0:
mem_probe_bank(base): write each probe offset (32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 MB, 0x20) as

leaves the SIMM size there. Returns the size, 0xff (empty) or 1/2 (the two
words differ).
blocks.0x7000769c:
mem_size_banks: probe the eight 32 MB banks (base n*0x02000000) with
mem_probe_bank and build %g2: bit 31 no bank yet, bit 30 memory found, bits
27:25 base of the lowest populated bank, bits [3n+2:3n] size code of bank n
(1 = 1 MB ... 6 = 32 MB).
blocks.0x70007774: mem_find_test_bank: highest populated bank -> %o0 base, %o1 size; -1 if none.
blocks.0x700098c0:
post_sequencer: runs the 55 POST tests in the order of the SS5 service manual's
"Full Diagnostic Mode Tests" table: MMU registers, TLB NTA, IOMMU group
(IOMMU, SBus/EBus time-outs), D-cache, I-cache, Memory Address Pattern, FPU
basic and CEXC groups, interrupts, timers, DMA2/LANCE/ESP/PPORT, NVRAM, TOD.
Caps Lock is toggled between groups (keyboard command 0x0e). The first failure
goes to post_fail_cpu_board / post_fail_cpu_board_leds (Num Lock),
post_fail_simm (Compose) or post_fail_nvram (Scroll Lock), each ending in
post_exit_soft_reset(2, message); all passed -> post_exit_soft_reset(0,
"Power-On Selftest PASSED").
blocks.0x70009cbc:
Dead code: follows the call to post_exit_soft_reset, which never returns
("Replace CPU Boot PROM" failure block of the removed EPROM checksum test).
blocks.0x70009e3c: Dead code: a second SIMM failure block after a post_exit_soft_reset call.
blocks.0x70009f00:
nta_march_test(%o0 base, %o1 length, %o2 stride, %o3 ASI, %o4 data mask): a
march test over any alternate space, through asi_st_word / asi_ld_word (ASI
dispatch stubs). Failures go to report_nta_error.
blocks.0x7000a55c:
mem_march_test(base, len, stride, mask, print_unum): address-in-address march:
up write addr; up read addr / write ~addr; down read ~addr. ASI 0x20 words.
blocks.0x7000aa60:
kbd_detect: keyboard reset (0x01), wait for 0xff, read the ID; ID 4 -> layout
request (0x0f), wait for 0xfe, read the layout. Returns 0 (none), 4, 5 or 9.
blocks.0x7000af64:
ASI dispatch: lda/sta take the ASI as an immediate, so these helpers index a
table of 49 two-instruction stubs (ba exit ; <op> [%i1] ASI) by ASI*8. Stores:
asi_st_word (sta), asi_st_half (stha), asi_st_byte (stba); load: asi_ld_word.
ASIs 0x21-0x2f use 0x20 (only one bypass ASI on microSPARC-II).
blocks.0x7000b88c: post_quiesce_leds_off: mask MA+T, %g1=0, system limit=0, LEDs off.
blocks.0x7000b8bc:
kbd_set_leds(v): keyboard command 0x0e followed by the LED mask (1 Num Lock,
2 Compose, 4 Scroll Lock, 8 Caps Lock).
blocks.0x7000b8d8: print_simm_unumber(addr): UNUMBER U0300..U0303 / U0400..U0403 by bank (addr bits 27:25).
blocks.0x7000bac0:
post_exit_soft_reset(%o0 status, %o1 message, %o2..%o5): the POST never
returns. It leaves %g1 = 'POST' (0x504f5354), %g2 = status (0 pass, 2 fail,
-1 not run), %g3 = 0xffd00010 + (message & 0x7ffff), %g4-%g7 = %o2-%o5, and
requests a software reset through the system control register; globals survive
the reset and obp_start_after_sw_reset picks them up.
blocks.0x7000bb24:
Software reset from boot space: jmp to boot-mode PC 0xbb40, which branches to
sysctl_soft_reset.
blocks.0x7000bb48:
reset_power_on: power-on path. ttya 9600 8N1, "Power-ON Reset", keyboard channel
1200 baud, processor 0 counter as user timer, keyboard reset (0x01) and scan:
no keyboard -> POST; Stop (0x01) -> skip POST; Stop-d (0x01 + 0x4f) -> set
diag-switch? (NVRAM 0x71200001 = 0xff) unless security-mode (NVRAM 0x7120004e)
is 1 or 2, and run POST; otherwise run POST only if diag-switch? is set.
blocks.0x7000bd98:
reset_entry: classify the reset with the system control/status register
(0x71f00000): bit 4 = watchdog reset -> reset_watchdog; bit 1 = software reset
(POST finished) -> reset_sw_reset; neither = power-on.
blocks.0x7000be18:
cache_init_enable: zero all I-cache tags (ASI 0xc, 32-byte lines, 16 KiB) and
D-cache tags (ASI 0xe, 16-byte lines, 8 KiB), then PCR |= IE|DE (0x300).
blocks.0x7000be70:
tlb_init_clear: zero the TLB diagnostic words ASI 6 0x000-0x1fc (PTEs and lower
tags) and 0x300-0x3fc (upper tags), and the TLB replacement control register.
blocks.0x7000bea8:
sysctl_soft_reset: write 1 (SW_RST) to the system control register. If the
reset does not happen, execution falls through into obp_start_after_sw_reset.
blocks.0x7000bec4:
obp_start_after_sw_reset: PSR = 0xfe0, WIM = 0, ttya init, pick up the POST
results if %g1 = 'POST' (else status -1), clear the TLB, clear and enable the
caches, then obp_cold_entry.
blocks.0x7000bf80:
watchdog_reenter_obp: flush the TLB, clear the level-15 interrupt, save the
context register (%l7) and set context 0, load TLB entries for the boot-mode
VA of this page, turn on the MMU and leave boot mode, then jump into the
Forth kernel's trap entry at 0xffd27c9c (through 0xffd0c0d8).
blocks.0x7000c120:
escc_wr_reg(%o0 = reg<<8 | value, %o1 = Z85C30 control port): write the
register pointer, then the value.
blocks.0x7000c28c:
boot_puts(%o0 = ROM offset): print a string on ttya, but only when NVRAM byte
0x71200001 (diag-switch?) is non-zero. Called with 0xffd0xxxx & 0x7ffff; ORs
0x70000000 back in and reads the bytes with lduba ASI 0x20.
blocks.0x7000c354:
kbd_getc_timeout: wait up to 0x3d090000 user-timer LSW units (1 s) for a
keyboard byte; returns it or -1.
blocks.0x7000c3e0:
Compiled C called from the Forth kernel (after the MMU is on): 64-bit memory
pattern tests (fill/check up/check down with ldda/stda ASI 0x20), printf
(%c %d %i %o %s %u %x) and a number printer.
blocks.0x7000c984:
mmu_build_boot_tables(%o0 = top of RAM region, %o1 = 0x1000): stackless (return
address kept in %sp). Allocates downwards from the top: 4 KiB context table,
context 0, CTPR, 64 KiB kernel RAM block, 1 KiB level-1 table; maps
0xffef0000 -> the RAM block (64 KiB), 0xffd00000 -> PROM (512 KiB) and
0x00000000 -> PROM (512 KiB). Returns the lowest allocated address.
blocks.0x7000cbd0:
mmu_map_range(%i0 pa, %i1 pa[35:32], %i2 va, %i3 size): for each 4 KiB page
walk/allocate the level-1/2/3 tables (256-byte level 2/3 tables) and write the
PTE ((pa >> 4) & 0x0fffff00) | space<<28 | 0x1e (ET=2, ACC=7, not cacheable).
blocks.0x7000f580:
c_get_unum(pa, flag): pointer to the J-number string of the SIMM bank holding
pa (table 0x7000f620, index pa >> 25), "?" for pa >= 0x10000000 or flag set.
c_mem_error_report prints the physical address, expected, observed and
U-number.
blocks.0x7002a86c:
obp_cold_entry (machine code inside the Forth region, reached from
obp_start_after_sw_reset). PSR = 0xfa0, WIM = 0; POST results into %i1..%i5;
find the highest 32 MB bank that holds 0x55555555/0xdeadbeef, size it by
aliasing, build the first page tables (mmu_build_boot_tables), turn the MMU
on and leave boot mode, TBR = 0xffeff000, move to the 0xffd00000 alias,
%g2 = Forth origin 0xffd15a00, copy the 0x980-byte RAM image from 0xffd3bd60 to
0xffef0000, store the memory size and POST results for Forth, and jump to the
inner interpreter at 0xffef0000 with IP %g5 = 0xffd1b33a.
